messages:
Maya (support): FYI @channel — we started getting a handful of 503s and lots of 429s right after the throttle policy canary went live (canary-id: canary-7). Reports from multiple customers on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. :rotating_light:
Maya (support): Example from customer A: 'requests returning 429: rate limit exceeded' + request id 0a7f3c. Customer B observed 503s with body 'upstream overloaded' around 10:12 UTC.
Maya (support): I pasted the two sample responses below:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: 0a7f3c
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "user-tier: standard, limit: 60rpm, burst: 120"
}
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-request-id: 1b9d8a
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "upstream_overloaded",
  "detail": "rate-limiter node errors: queue_depth=512, dropped=47"
}
```

Alex (eng-platform): Thanks Maya. Was the canary a pure config push (policy delta) or did this include code in the rate-limiter?
Maya (support): Policy-only push via console. The change tightened burst windows for non-enterprise keys and enabled the new token-bucket enforcement in front of the GPU pools. Canary target was 2% traffic, started at 10:05 UTC.
Sam (eng-sre): telemetry-bot, can you post the error-rate and 429/503 counts for the canary cohorts vs baseline for the last 30m?
telemetry-bot: Canary (canary-7) metrics: error_rate jumped from 0.3% -> 3.9% after rollout. 429 count: baseline 14 -> canary 480. 503 count: baseline 2 -> canary 24. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rl/rollout-canary-7
Alex (eng-platform): Ok. Looks like requests are getting mapped to the stricter policy unexpectedly or the limiter pool is backing up. Two likely suspects: (1) header parsing / tier lookup failing -> keys default to 'standard' which has lower limits; (2) enforcement-layer (rate-limiter pods) mis-sized for the enforcement pattern and queue depth spiked.
Sam (eng-sre): I'm seeing logs from rate-limiter-2 that show repeated EADDRINUSE-ish connection retries and a lot of renew failures. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:11:23Z rate-limiter-2 ERROR failed to refresh policy snapshot: rpc timeout
2026-03-15T10:11:24Z rate-limiter-2 WARN token-bucket overflow drop=12
2026-03-15T10:11:26Z rate-limiter-2 ERROR upstream: accept: resource temporarily unavailable
```

Sam (eng-sre): That explains the 503. For 429s we need to confirm whether client-tier lookup returned unexpected values. Alex, do we have a canary toggle to revert to previous policy quickly?
Alex (eng-platform): Yes, rollback endpoint available. I can flip the canary selector to route 0% to canary and back to baseline. Rolling it back should immediately stop policy delta enforcement. Deploy-bot: policy canary push complete (canary-id=canary-7, rollout=2%).
Maya (support): Customers are asking for ETA. Jordan (customer-success), can you draft a short note?
Jordan (customer-success): On it. I can message the top 10 affected customers within 10m once we confirm rollback.
Alex (eng-platform): Plan: (1) I will set canary to 0% now. (2) Sam please check rate-limiter pods and restart the problematic node(s). (3) telemetry-bot watch for error_rate to fall back to baseline. If error_rate doesn't drop within 5m after rollback, we escalate to full rollback of the policy (manual config restore).
Sam (eng-sre): Restarting rate-limiter-2 now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter -n infra --selector=pod=rate-limiter-2`
Sam (eng-sre): Also bumping replicas from 3 -> 5 temporarily for the enforcement tier to drain queues.
Alex (eng-platform): Flipping canary -> 0% now (console action).
deploy-bot: canary update: canary-7 traffic -> 0% (actor: alex, at 10:14:02 UTC)
telemetry-bot: Observability: 2m after rollback, error_rate for cohort dropped to 0.5%, 429s down to 26, 503s down to 3.
Maya (support): Thanks. I told the queued customers we're reverting and will follow up in ~10m.
Maya (support): Repro steps (for eng) appended for local testing:
1) Use a non-enterprise test key (tier=standard).
2) Run a burst test: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done`
Expected: some 429s at high concurrency. Current: 429s start earlier and 503s appear after ~60s.
Alex (eng-platform): Action items tracked: Alex -> canary toggle (done), Sam -> pod restart + capacity bump (in progress), Maya/Jordan -> customer comms.
Sam (eng-sre): Rate-limiter-2 restarted and back to healthy. Replica bump completed. Watching logs and queue depth.
Sam (eng-sre): Logs now show normal accept rates and policy snapshot refresh OK. No more overflow drops.
telemetry-bot: Final: 15m window error_rate = 0.4% (within baseline), 429 total for window = 32, 503 total = 4.
Maya (support): Closing loop with customers now. Jordan will post follow-ups and offer credit if they saw significant disruption.
Jordan (customer-success): I'll reach out with the note + we should attach a short RCA when available.
Alex (eng-platform): Postmortem: let's capture root cause as a mismatch between policy rollout (tighter burst windows) + transient rate-limiter node instability exposing queue backpressure. Action: add canary smoke test to run a 1m burst and assert queue_depth < 50, plus a safe-fallback that defaults to previous policy when rate-limiter RPC timeouts exceed threshold.
Maya (support): Thanks everyone. Closing thread once Jordan confirms customer messages sent. :white_check_mark:
